name: Chisholm Trail
desc: A 9 mile paved ribbon that cuts straight through central Plano along a creek, linking Jack Carter, Big Lake and Memorial Park without you ever touching a road. Bike it end to end or just pick a shady creek section and walk. Golden hour is the move, the tree cover keeps it cool when the rest of Plano is baking.

reviews.text: Best long ride in Plano, barely any road crossings.
Shady and smooth. Gets busy Saturday mornings.

name: Bob Woodruff Park
desc: Big quiet park on Rowlett Creek with fishing ponds, sand volleyball courts and a seven acre fenced dog park. Bring a hammock and a speaker, claim a shaded picnic table, and wander the trail that connects over to Oak Point. Weekday evenings it feels like you have the whole place to yourself.

reviews.text: Volleyball courts plus a pond, unbeatable combo.
Dog park is huge and actually shaded.

name: Jack Carter Park
desc: Sits right where the Bluebonnet and Chisholm trails meet, so it doubles as a proper trailhead and a hangout. There is an all abilities playground, a pool, open fields for spikeball and a dog park off the trail. Easiest place to meet friends before a long ride.

reviews.text: Perfect meetup spot before hitting Chisholm.
Big open grass, great for frisbee at sunset.

name: Carpenter Park
desc: North Plano park with a rec center, wide open fields and paved paths that spill into the neighborhood greenbelt system. Good for a lazy loop walk, a pickup game or laying out on the grass with food from Coit. Go late afternoon when the light hits the tree line.

reviews.text: Clean, big, and never packed on weekdays.
Nice easy loop when I do not want a real hike.

name: Hoblitzelle Park
desc: An underrated older park just east of downtown with mature shade trees, a pond and trails that link into the east side creek system. It is small and low key, which is the point. Walk over after wandering the Arts District and you will probably have a bench to yourself.

reviews.text: My quiet reading spot, nobody is ever here.
Great shade, easy walk from downtown.

name: Preston Ridge Trail
desc: Long paved north to south trail on the west side that threads past Windhaven and the Preston corridor, mostly separated from traffic. It is the flattest, fastest stretch in Plano for a run or a skate. Best right after sunrise or once the sun drops behind the tree line.

reviews.text: Smoothest pavement in the city, no lie.
Long enough for a real workout without loops.

name: Windhaven Meadows Park
desc: Rolling open meadow park in west Plano with wide sky, a pond and paved paths that tie into Preston Ridge Trail. Almost no tree cover in the middle, which makes it the best sunset spot on this side of town. Bring a blanket and go about an hour before dark.

reviews.text: Sunsets here are stupid good.
Open and breezy, dogs love it.

name: Interurban Railway Museum
desc: Tiny free museum in the old Texas Electric Railway station in downtown Plano where you can climb into a restored interurban rail car and see the original ticket window. Takes maybe thirty minutes and it is a genuinely weird cool piece of North Texas history. Pair it with a walk around the brick streets outside.

reviews.text: Free, small, and way cooler than expected.
Climbing in the old car is the whole thing.

name: ArtCentre of Plano
desc: Rotating local art shows inside the restored Saigling House, a 1918 home turned gallery on the edge of the Arts District. Free to walk through, and the porch and grounds are a nice place to sit after. Check their calendar, opening nights are when the place actually gets loud.

reviews.text: Beautiful old house, real local artists.
Small but the rotating shows keep it fresh.

name: Courtyard Theater
desc: A 321 seat theater in a converted downtown school building that runs the Courtyard Texas Music Series plus plays and touring acts. Small enough that every seat feels close to the stage. Grab dinner on 15th Street first and walk over.

reviews.text: No bad seats, sound is great.
Texas Music Series nights are worth it.

name: Josey Records Plano
desc: Deep crates of new and used vinyl, CDs, tapes and posters tucked into a strip on Coit. You can lose an hour flipping through the dollar bins alone and the staff will actually talk to you about what you are buying. Go on a weekday when it is quiet enough to dig properly.

reviews.text: Dollar bins are dangerous, found three keepers.
Staff recs are always solid.

name: Movement Plano
desc: A 32,000 square foot climbing gym with 5,000 feet of bouldering and ropes running up to 55 feet, plus a Kilter and Moon Board. Day passes and rentals mean you can show up with zero gear and zero experience. Weeknights after work get packed, so aim for a late morning or Sunday evening session.

reviews.text: Setting is fun and the walls are tall.
Rented shoes, got hooked immediately.

name: Plano Antique Mall
desc: Multi vendor antique mall right in downtown packed with vintage furniture, old signage, jewelry and genuine oddities. It is a maze and the fun is finding the one weird thing nobody else has. Best on a slow Saturday afternoon when you can browse without rushing.

reviews.text: Found a 70s lamp I think about daily.
Booths change often, always worth a lap.

name: Holman Pottery
desc: Working pottery studio and gallery in the Arts District where you can watch pieces being thrown and buy straight off the shelf. They run classes and open studio times if you want to actually get clay on your hands. Time your visit with a downtown art walk and it becomes a whole afternoon.

reviews.text: Watching them throw is oddly hypnotic.
Bought two mugs, use them every day.
